chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn Fudayl, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married off his male slave to his female slave, then he divorced her with two divorces. If the master wished, would he remarry her? He said: No. I said: What if the master had sexual intercourse with her? Would it be permissible for the slave to remarry her? He said: No, until she marries another husband, and he consummates the marriage with her, so that the marriage is like the first marriage. And if he had divorced her with one divorce, and the master wished, he would remarry her.

key_terms.نِكَاحًا مِثْلَ نِكَاحِ الْأَوَّلِ: A marriage like the first marriage (implying full consummation and validity)
key_terms.وَطِئَهَا: He had sexual intercourse with her
key_terms.يُرَاجِعُهَا: He remarries her (without a new contract)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a master and a slave to remarry each other after divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the legal autonomy of slaves in marital matters, establishing that their divorce and remarriage rules mirror those of free persons. It specifically addresses the 'two divorces' scenario, ruling that the master cannot simply remarry the slave woman without her undergoing a valid intermediate marriage (Nikah Mithl) and consummation, thereby preventing the master from retaining full control over her marital status. This ruling underscores the principle that while the master owns the slave, the marital bond is subject to standard Islamic jurisprudence regarding revocable and irrevocable divorces.
